name: CHEROKEE COUNTY

fact.summary: The same EPA fact sheet says the OU5 cleanup remedy does not address potential future residential development in that area, which limits reuse of OU5 for housing under the current remedy. Institutional controls limit land use on capped waste areas.
fact.reference: Cherokee County NPL Superfund Site (Kansas), EPA site page
fact.quote: The OU5 remedy does not address the potential future residential development of the area.

verifier_note: Page says 'The OU5 remedy does not address the potential future residential development of the area.' and ICs 'limit land use on capped waste areas' (OU3/4/6). 'Limits reuse of OU5 for housing' is the researcher's inference.

name: SANGAMON ORDNANCE PLANT

fact.summary: Illinois EPA fact sheet 4 (May 2005) on the Formosa Plastics site west of Illiopolis, the former Borden PVC plant within the ordnance plant land. The state did not yet know the extent of the chemicals left on site, and it said the remedial investigation would not fully start until demolition was complete. The sheet is about 20 years old, and no later agency status was found.
fact.reference: Formosa Plastics site, Illiopolis: Illinois EPA fact sheet 4
fact.quote: The Illinois EPA does not yet know the extent of chemicals that remain.

verifier_note: Page is May 2005 IEPA fact sheet 4 on the Formosa Plastics plant, Illiopolis; both quotes present. But it never mentions Borden or the Sangamon Ordnance Plant, so link to this FUDS site is not shown.

name: CHARLOTTE ARMY MIS PL

fact.summary: Charlotte City Council approved a rezoning for the 72-acre Camp North End development in September 2017. The county landmark record names this site the Charlotte Area Missile Plant at 300 Camp Road. At the time, ATCO's plans called for up to 1,500 apartments and 1.5 million square feet of office space.
fact.reference: Council approves 72-acre Camp North End rezoning
fact.quote: The Charlotte City Council on Monday approved a rezoning for the 72-acre Camp North End development

verifier_note: Rezoning of 72-acre Camp North End, 1,500 apartments, 1.5M sq ft office are on the page. But 'county landmark record names this site Charlotte Area Missile Plant at 300 Camp Road' is not; page names neither.

name: WINSTON-SALEM ARPT

fact.summary: Signature Aviation reopened a renovated fixed-base operator (FBO) of about 3,000 sq ft in the airport terminal, which dates to 1941. The reconstruction took two years. The article reports a completed tenant renovation, not a redevelopment of former Army airfield land. The FUDS record name is Winston-Salem Airport, matched here to Smith Reynolds Airport by name and airport history.
fact.reference: Signature Debuts Updated North Carolina FBO
fact.quote: celebrating the grand reopening of its renovated FBO this week at Smith Reynolds Airport (KINT)

verifier_note: Page says Signature reopened renovated FBO at Smith Reynolds Airport (KINT), 2025-08-14, ~3,000 sq ft, terminal 1941. No Army/FUDS mention; link to the FUDS record rests on name only.

name: CAMP HOWZE

fact.summary: KXII reports the groundbreaking of Camp Howze Industrial Rail Park on June 18, 2026. KXII gives 480 acres; the developer's release gives 489 acres. The developer's release says the park is planned for up to 7 million square feet across 14 buildings. The park is a part of the former camp, not the whole 58,702-acre FUDS property.
fact.reference: Groundbreaking held for Camp Howze Industrial Rail Park in Gainesville
fact.quote: 480-acre development just off Interstate 35 in northwest Gainesville.

verifier_note: Page gives 480 acres off I-35, groundbreaking 2026-06-18. No mention of the former Camp Howze or military history, so 'part of the former camp' is not shown.

name: IOWA ARMY AMMUNITION PLANT

fact.summary: The Commerce Center of Southeast Iowa is a 152.9-acre certified industrial site on federal land inside the plant, near Middletown. An act of Congress raised the land lease from 25 to 50 years to allow the site. The site is also BNSF rail-served certified. Partners named in the 2016 certification are the Iowa Economic Development Authority, the Greater Burlington Partnership and American Ordnance.
fact.reference: Burlington-area site joins 11 sites in Iowa that are part of the Iowa Certified Site program
fact.quote: it took an act of Congress to increase the lease duration on the land from the normal 25 years to 50 years.

verifier_note: Page supports 152.9 acres, federal land in plant, Congress lease 25 to 50 yrs. But BNSF rail, Greater Burlington Partnership and American Ordnance do not appear on the page, which the fact asserts.
